TX.grade_reason: Bulk, free, no login. The nightly Drilling Permit Master and Trailer file has one record per permit and amendment with the issue (approval) date, received date, application type, depth, county, district, operator number and spud date; the monthly and End of Month files give the history. This site already builds monthly and daily permit counts from it.
TX.producer_plan: Already built (d1 monthly, d7 daily). Monthly: read the Drilling Permit Master and Trailer (daf802), keep record 02 per permit number, count by issue month; new drill is application type 01 (first record per permit number with a valid issue date). Other bands by the same type code: 07 re-enter, 14 recomplete, 15 reclass, 09 field transfer; amendments are the records with a sequence number below 99 or an amended date. Injection and disposal appear only as W-1s whose field well code is I or D (record 03); permits for injection wells on other UIC forms were not examined. Daily: the plain daf420.dat (current month, lags one business day) plus month-end files for earlier months, and the twice-daily pending sets for the queue. Caveats: the permit file stores an internal district code; coordinates in the file cover only part of recent permits (4 to 39 percent in several months of 2026), so counts never come from the dots (the RRC map layer fills them in); the dated snapshots turn to a new month on the 3rd; a file holds one month plus earlier permits touched that month.
TX.privacy: The permit files hold operator names and numbers (some operators are individuals, so this site names only P-5 corporations, LLCs and limited partnerships), an alternate-address record, and in the pending set the operator's mailing address and phone columns.

OK.grade_reason: Free, no login, open to anyone. The Intent to Drill master and 7-day workbooks have one row per application with an approval date, submit date, application type (drill, recomplete, re-enter, deepen, amend), well class and surface location, and the master goes back to 1999. This site already builds monthly and daily counts from them. Caveat: many permit columns are 0 or blank in current rows, and the files are Excel, not CSV.
OK.producer_plan: Already built (d8_ok_monthly weekly, d8_ok_daily nightly). Read the Intent to Drill master workbook (154 MB, about 70 s with this site's own stream reader) and the 7-day file; keep Application_Type DR with an Approval_Date for new drills, and fold rows (one per formation until mid-2025) to one permit per first ten API digits and Central approval day; Approval_Date is a UTC Excel serial, so convert to Central days before counting by month. Other bands by the same column: RC recomplete, RE re-enter, DP deepen (other), AM amend (left out of permit counts, counted as amended), and injection or disposal by Well_Class (DIS, SWD, INJ, DNC) among the approved rows. REJ and DEL rows are excluded. Caveats: the 7-day file ends the day before it is made (about 00:41 UTC), so a morning run reads the master for the gap; Drill_Type and Formation_* are blank, so horizontals cannot be counted from permits (depth is the proxy); an approval dated in the future is a typo to skip.
OK.privacy: The Intent to Drill files carry operator address columns, the submitting person's name, phone and fax columns (and the dictionary lists an e-mail column), and the well and lease-like names; this site reads none of them and names operators only when they are corporations, LLCs or limited partnerships. Form 1000's contacts tab takes a name, phone and e-mail.

AK.grade_reason: The Data Miner's two 'ZIP (All Data)' exports are free, need no login and answer a plain automated request. The Well Work Dates file holds every dated event of every Permit to Drill (application received, approved, issued, spudded, completed), and the Wells file holds the class, status, area, field, depths, locations and elevations, so monthly approvals can be counted from 2019. Limits: the Commission gives every sidetrack and lateral leg its own permit (90 to 190 permits a year, about half for new holes), no recompletion or plug-back permit is dated, and no proposed depth is published. Updated 2026-11-01: both files were opened and a producer reads them weekly; its 2020 count (89 permits, 36 Arctic Slope oil wells) equals the Commission's own chart exactly, and 2018 is 3 percent above its count.
AK.producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_ak.py. Two requests 3 s apart to the Data Miner's own export files (wellhistory.zip, wells.zip), read whole each run (about 9 s; the workbook uses prefixed XML tags, so the producer has its own small reader). Counts Permits to Drill by the 'Dt Well Permit Approved' event, one per permit, from 2019. Bands from the sidetrack digits of the well number and the class the permit was issued for: new = original hole of a Development or Exploratory permit; inj = original hole of a Service well; redrill = any sidetrack or lateral code; other = Stratigraphic Test; rework and amend are null (recompletions are sundry notices; 'Re-Issued' is not read as an amendment). Fluid from PermittedStatus; places are the Commission's areas. Refuses: a stale export (over 45 days), no approval in 45 days, a changed header, over 2% of approvals with no class, approvals and issues over 40% apart, a history over 10% smaller than the committed one. A 401, 403, 407 or 429 exits 2 and keeps the file.
AK.privacy: The files name operators (companies and a few agencies; the producer names only corporations, LLCs and partnerships) and carry a Leases column that can hold a landowner's name (never published). Scanned permits to drill and plats can name landowners and staff contacts: link nothing from them.

AZ.grade_reason: A free and open ArcGIS layer with one row per permitted or drilled well (permit number, API, operator, county, TRS, lat/long, depth, formation, spud date, status and status date), updated in 2026. It has no approval or filing date: the only dates are spud, end of drilling and the date of the current status, so monthly permit counts are approximate. Volume is small (about 80 permits since 2020, mostly helium in Apache County, plus geothermal in Greenlee).
AZ.producer_plan: Query the layer (where=1=1, outFields=*, returnGeometry=false; 1,288 rows, 2 MB, under the 2,000-row limit) once a night or week and keep each snapshot, because the layer is a current-state table. A permit counts as new in the first snapshot where its PERMIT_ID appears (numbers are sequential: 1317 in Sep 2025, 1324 in Jul 2026), and the approval can be dated by the first snapshot with STATUS_WELL = Permitted and the STATUS_DATE then shown. For history before the first snapshot, STATUS_DATE of rows still at Permitted, Permit Extension or Permit Expired is a rough date; SPUD_DATE gives wells spudded by month (New Mexico style). Activity types come from WELL_TYPE and COMMODITY (oil and gas, helium, CO2, geothermal, storage); new drill versus re-entry is not in the layer (NOTES text such as 'reapply for permit AZOGCC:1271' marks a reissue). The exact approval date is in each approval-letter PDF's file name on the per-well page (azogcc.az.gov/<permit>), but those PDFs sit behind a Cloudflare challenge that refused this machine, so they may refuse a GitHub runner too. Expect 0 to 15 permits a year.
AZ.privacy: The layer has OPERATOR, PRIOR_OPERATOR, DRILLER and MINERAL_OWNER, which can hold individuals or private landowners and the AGOL EDITOR and LAST_EDITED_USER columns hold staff user names; do not publish them without a corporate-name filter. AR.grade_reason: The weekly Permit and Completion Reports are free workbooks (PDFs before mid-2020), one a Friday since January 2019, listing every Form 2 drilling permit with its operator, county, field, location, proposed depth, zone and a printed purpose (original, renewal, amendment, re-entry). Held to B, not A: the date is the week of issue, not the day; there is no well type, so disposal, brine and carbon-storage wells sit among the new permits; five weeks are missing; and the files are reached through an ASP.NET page. The GIS wells layer has well types but no permit date and has not been updated since late 2025. Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the reports each week; new plus re-entry permits account for 308 of the 312 permit numbers assigned from 2019 to 2025, and exactly for 2024 and 2025.
AR.producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_ar.py. Posts the year to the reports page (form state from the first GET, no cookie), reads the file names from the tree and GETs each report by its static address (xlsx since mid-2020; PDFs through pdftotext before), 3 s apart, up to four tries a file. Only the two Form 2 sections are read. A week counts in the month that holds its Wednesday. Bands: no purpose printed = new; renewal or amend = amend; re-entry = redrill; any other word = other; inj, rework and fluid are null (no well type on the list). The county comes from the API number's county place (the printed county cell moves); the API number is read only for that, never kept. A weekly run reads the last 14 months (62 requests, about 4 minutes) and takes older months from the committed file. Limits: seven repeated listings (new up to 2% high), five missing weeks (KNOWN_MISSING), permit numbers typed with mistakes (never a key). Checks are in NOTES_D11.md.
AR.privacy: Form 2 asks the send-to street address, e-mail and phone; none of these are in the weekly reports or the GIS layer. The reports and the layer list operators; seven listings since 2019 are a person's or a family firm's and are never named.

ID.grade_reason: Idaho issues about one permit to drill a year (8 since 2019). Every well it has permitted has a free page with its status, county, operator, proposed depths and the signed Permit to Drill, whose file name starts with the date. Held to B, not A: there is no bulk file or API with the date, it comes from the file names of 34 pages (two amended permits needed their first approval read from the signed letters), and the Data Explorer's 'Date Issued' is not reliable. Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the pages each week (35 requests) and its permits match the Commission's own quarterly 'APDs Approved' counts month by month from 2021 to mid-2025; the Data Explorer does answer without a login (a JSON search and a public map layer), but neither holds a trustworthy approval date.
ID.producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_id.py. Reads the well index and each well's page (35 requests, 3 s apart, about 2.5 minutes, plain automated agent, no refusal) and counts one permit per well by the date at the start of its 'Permit to Drill' file name, from 2019 (only the new band; every other band and the fluid are null: the Commission posts no dated list of amendments, well treatments or injection permits). ORIGINAL_APPROVAL holds the two dates of permits whose posted file is the amended permit, keyed by the amended file's date and held to the page's creation date. ND.grade_reason: The only free bulk or API source (the Wells map layer, 44,030 wells) has a spud date, well type and status but no approval date or work type, so by the grading rule it measures spuds. The approval dates exist only in the free Daily Activity Report text PDFs (one per business day since 1997, well-level, with section headings that give the activity type) and in the monthly statistics PDF (aggregate). Those make approvals countable, but from PDFs, which the rubric rates C; the well index Excel file is paid.
ND.producer_plan: Approvals and activity types: read the Daily Activity Report PDFs (one per business day, a per-year folder, file name drMMDDYY.pdf, about 150 KB, text-based; pdftotext -layout worked on two 2026 reports). Treat the report date as the approval day (assumption: not checked against the filing system). Each entry starts '#fileno - OPERATOR, well name, location, county...'. Count entries by heading: PERMITS APPROVED = new drill; PERMITTED FOR RECOMPLETION = recomplete; PERMIT MODIFICATION (surface hole location, spacing unit change) = amend; PERMIT RENEWALS, PERMIT CANCELLATIONS, CHANGE OF OPERATOR and RELEASED FROM CONFIDENTIAL STATUS = other (never count renewals as new). Injection and disposal permits have no heading of their own: join the file number to the Wells layer well_type (SWD, WI, GI and similar) or read SWD in the well name; whether such permits appear under PERMITS APPROVED was not verified. Only two reports were read, so check the headings against a sample from each year before trusting a long history; be polite (a pause between files, a few hundred files a night at most).
ND.privacy: The layers and daily reports name operators (companies) and wells; no individual's name was seen in the fields read, but an operator can be an individual or carry a 'DBA' name, so apply the project's name rule before publishing. The blank forms ask for operator telephone and e-mail, surface-owner names and addresses; those are filed data, not published in the layers or reports read.

TN.grade_reason: The Division's table of every oil and gas well permit since 1968 (16,614 rows) is free and shown two ways, a Data Viewer report and a map layer behind its Map Viewer, with the same eleven columns: API number, permit number, permit date, operator, well name, county, coordinates, elevation, formation at total depth and purpose of well. Held to B, not A: the table's only date is the permit date, read as the issue date without a TDEC definition; it has no type of permit, and the purpose of well is the outcome (three permits in four are dry holes), not what was applied for; the Division updates it monthly; and its servers refuse a generic automated agent (403) and answer one that names itself. Updated 2026-11-01: a producer reads the layer weekly in two requests; the viewer and the layer give the same total and yearly counts, though no count from a second system was found.
TN.producer_plan: Built: d11_nat_tn.py. Reads the Oil_and_Gas2 layer 0 in two requests 3 s apart (a statistics count, then one query of the 11 columns: the whole table is under maxRecordCount 17,000), sending the one honest agent string the host accepts (HEADERS in the producer). Counts every permit by PERMIT_DATE (a calendar day at midnight UTC: a layer that stores any other moment fails the run); new is every permit, a service or test purpose (none issued since 2014) would be left out of new and told in the note; inj, redrill, rework, amend and other are null (no type of permit; the purpose is an outcome). Fluid from the purpose (Oil, Oil And Gas, Gas and Shut-in Gas; a dry hole, a location not drilled and NCG are unknown). The last 60 days are not shown (the Division updates monthly and gaps between permits reach 98 days); asOf is the day of the read. Operators are named only if a corporation, LLC or partnership. Guards: an error reply, a renamed column, under 15,000 rows, fewer than 150 permits since 2019, dates not at midnight, holes in the numbering over 5%, a purpose never seen, a newest permit over a year old. The Data Viewer gives the same rows if the layer goes away.
TN.privacy: The table names operators; a few permits are in a person's name (never published: the producer names only corporations, LLCs and partnerships). It holds no street address or phone number, but it has coordinates and well names, which the producer never asks for.

VA.producer_plan: Option 1, history: query layer 0 (Active Wells) in pages of 2000 and count FiDrComp (drilling complete) and FiWellComp (well completion) by month, split by TblOpDesc; this measures wells drilled or completed, like New Mexico's spuds, with a lag. Wells leave layer 4 when drilled, so history cannot be rebuilt from it. Check whether FiStatDt on an 'Issued' row is the issue date (many fall on the same day in pairs and threes, which looks like batches, but this is not confirmed). Option 3: the DGO Inquiry 'Permit Issuance' and 'Permit Issuance Statistics' reports, if they give issue dates; they need an ASP.NET form post, which is fragile. The VGOB service is not started. Work type is not a field (new vs modification is separate layers: Pending Wells vs Pending Well Modifications).

WV.grade_reason: Two free bulk sources open to anyone without login: the weekly permit reports (a real list of each week's permit actions since 2019: API, action Issued or Modification or Cancelled or WR-35_approved, permit type, well type, operator, county) and the TAGIS map service (one row per well with exact issue date and received date, permit type, well type, status, coordinates, 154,247 rows). Counts of one week matched in both. Two weaknesses: the weekly list has no date column (only the week in the file name), and the layer keeps only each well's latest permit, so older new-drill permits can drop out (2019 week: 9 of 10) and modifications are missing.
WV.producer_plan: Use both. (1) Recent and exact: query the MapServer layer 7 with where issuedate between the first and last day of the month and group by permittype (and welltype); paginate with resultOffset (3,000 per page); dates are yyyy/mm/dd text so string comparison works; no geometry needed. New Drill = new; Re-Drill and Partial Plug Re-drill = reentry; Re-Work, Drilling Deeper, Fracture = recomplete; UIC Permit, Convert, Brine Disposal, Secondary Recovery Well = injection; Plugging, Partial Plug, Storage, General Permit, Emergency Permit and older labels = other. (2) Complete action counts since 2019: download each Weekly Permit Report zip from the archive folders (one zip per week, name 'Weekly Permit Report MM-DD-YYYY'), read the xlsx (stdlib zip and XML), keep rows by Permit_Action: Issued = permits issued, Modification = amend, Cancelled = withdrawn, WR-35_approved = completion approvals; map Permit Type as above. Put a week in the month of its Monday, or split it by the layer's issue dates.
WV.privacy: The weekly list and the layer name operators (a few may be individuals) and the layer's farm name is the form's 'Farm Name/Surface Owner' item, which can be a landowner's surname; the forms collect owner and neighbor names and addresses, which are not published in the data. WY.grade_reason: Free, no login, open to anyone. The approved-permits export returns one row per permit/well with an Approved date (yyyymmdd), a received date, well class, horizontal flag, location and spud date, by any date range. Strictly it has no work-type column, so counts mix new drills with re-entries, deepenings and renewals (a B under a strict reading of the rubric).
WY.producer_plan: Use the WOGCC approved-permits export (POST https://pipeline.wyo.gov/DumpByApdA.cfm with bmon,bday,byear,emon,eday,eyear and cType: 1 all permitted, 2 oil and gas, 3 coal bed, 4 injector/disposal, 5 horizontal, 9 waiting on approval). One request per month (or one per week for the nightly) returns an .xls that is really an HTML table: parse it with the standard library, header row first, one data row per permit. Month = the Approved column (yyyymmdd). Count rows per month per Well_Class (codes seen in the well header: O, G, GO, OO oil and gas; I and D injection or disposal; MW, ST, M monitor and test; coal bed wells are asked for separately with cType 3 and carry old numeric classes such as 05, so decide whether to include them). Dir/Hor 'H' marks horizontals (seen in the sample); a drilled-but-not-yet-spud permit has a blank Spud_Date. Cross-check with the monthly well-header zip (RECDATE received counts, FIRSTSPUD, STATUS).
WY.privacy: Company column holds operator names (some may be individuals; apply this site's corporation/LLC/LP rule before naming one). The exports carry no phone, e-mail or street address. Form 1 itself collects a contact person, phone and e-mail, and the surface owner's details go on Form 1A; none of that is in the data files. Nothing copied.

FF.grade_reason: Bulk, free and open, with every fractured well in the country in one download: its point, county, the job's start and end days, depth, water and every chemical. It holds no permit and no approval date, so it cannot count permits: it records the fracturing job, filed after it, not the permit. The download page says the data are as the operator filed them and that corrections are approved by the state agencies that require a disclosure.
FF.producer_plan: Already built. The Overview's map and the Daily report read the disclosure list by range requests (d13_newwells.py, data/newwells/), and build_db.py --fracfocus loads the whole registry with its water sources into the local database; the ingredients are only in the local database (about 2.5 GB). A disclosure comes weeks to months after the permit, so it is shown beside the permit counts and never added into them.
FF.privacy: The registry names API numbers and well names, and some operators are people. The site publishes none of those from it: the map holds a well's point, county, day, depth and water, and an operator only when it is a corporation, LLC or limited partnership. The local database snapshot holds the registry as filed (README, Privacy).
